classification.vuln_type: segfault on exhausted fixed-size buffer pool (allocation failure not handled)
classification.impact: DoS (UPF crash on 9-th consecutive Session Establishment)

trigger.message: 9-th (or later) consecutive PFCP Session Establishment Request without resetting NFs
trigger.ie_path: N/A (resource-creating request; the bug is in per-session buffer allocation)
trigger.field: bufPool64 (fixed-size 64-byte buffer pool in utlt_buff). PFCP-Session-Establishment-related buffers are never freed across consecutive establishments, so the pool drains after ~8 sessions. SelectBufblkOption logs 'bufPool64 is empty' and returns failure; downstream code dereferences the failed allocation -> segfault. PC1 'Resource Exhaustion' — bounded pool exhausted by resource-creating requests, no graceful failure path.
trigger.precondition: PFCP association established; multiple consecutive SERs without NF restart

ground_truth.crash_type: ERRO 'bufPool64 is empty' (utlt_buff.c:80 SelectBufblkOption) immediately followed by Segmentation fault on the failed-allocation pointer

root_cause.note: SelectBufblkOption returns failure when bufPool64 is empty; the caller does not check the return and dereferences the (NULL/invalid) bufblk pointer -> segfault. Pool size is hard-coded in utlt_buff and the per-session buffers are not released.

call_stack: (per-session buffer allocator, caller not in stack but dereferences failed alloc)
